reproduction_target: Pan-cancer secondary analysis of PCAWG/ICGC whole-genome and transcriptome data joined with TCMA mtDNA copy-number data: mtDNA copy-number computation in normal samples (bedtools coverage ratio), mutation mapping and functional classification (promoter/coding/intronic-UTR/intergenic on GRCh37), purity filtering and median normalization, Spearman correlation of mtDNA copy number with mutational load, predictive models (linear regression, Ridge via the R 'ridge' package, Lasso via 'glmnet', randomForest), differential expression between high- and low-mtDNA samples with DESeq2 at gene and transcript level, PCA (PCAtools), volcano plots (EnhancedVolcano), heatmaps (pheatmap), alternative-splicing inference from differential transcripts, functional/pathway enrichment with g:Profiler (GO/KEGG/Reactome), MSigDB hallmark and EMTome signature analyses, MT-CO2-based regression prediction of hallmark gene expression, and a chemotherapy-resistance likelihood score. No wet-lab work is reported: all data are consortium-derived, so W = 0 and every step is computational.
granularity_note: Coarse one-step-per-named-tool/analysis, built from the bioRxiv v1 JATS XML Methods section (retrieved by curl with a browser User-Agent; WebFetch of the .source.xml returned HTTP 403). Methods subsections used: Dataset; Mutation mapping and functional classification; Correlation analysis of mtDNA copy number with mutational load; Linear regression and random forest models for prediction of mtDNA copy number; Differential expression analysis of genes and transcripts between high- and low-mtDNA samples; Pathway enrichment and analysis of signature gene sets; Regression models for predicting expression of hallmark gene sets; Calculation of likelihood score for chemotherapy resistance. The Code availability statement names one public repository (https://github.com/riddhimandhar/Cancer_mtDNAcn); its landing page and README were read at PROSE level only (folder-to-analysis mapping), no script source was read — that is Stage 2. The repository has no releases and no tags, and its file listing contains no environment, lockfile, conda spec, Dockerfile, renv, or sessionInfo artifact. Ploidy-correction scripts present in the repository (C13/C14) have no counterpart in the Methods prose and are therefore not counted as steps.

steps.label: Acquisition of PCAWG consensus mutation data from the ICGC data portal (high-quality consensus SNVs/MNVs/small INDELs passing PCAWG quality filtering, plus consensus SVs, consensus CNVs, mutational signatures including APOBEC, tumor purity from consensus CNV calls, and clinical/histology first-therapy-type and first-therapy-response data) — no PCAWG/ICGC data release version, no download date, no file-level accession

Acquisition of tumor mtDNA copy number and mtDNA SNVs/indels from The Cancer Mitochondria Atlas (TCMA, https://bioinformatics.mdanderson.org/public-software/tcma/) — public resource, no release version or download date stated

Genome-wide read-coverage computation on aligned WGS/WXS reads of normal tissue, normal blood and other normal samples with bedtools, and derivation of normal-sample mtDNA copy number as the mtDNA-to-nuclear coverage ratio (repo folder 0_normal_data_mtDNA_CN: C1_normSamp_calc_coverage_WgsWxs.pl, C2_stats_normSamp_coverage_WgsWxs.pl) — no bedtools version, no command line, no coverage/mappability thresholds

Mutation mapping and functional classification into promoter (5' flanking, within 1000 bp upstream of the start codon), coding (truncating = frameshift indels + nonsense; strong-effect = in-frame indels + missense; silent), intronic/UTR and intergenic classes on the GRCh37 assembly (repo 1_mutation_data_processing: C2_process_PCAWG_mito_data_v2.pl, C3_SNP_indel_data_cat_with_prom_v2.pl)

Purity filtering (tumor purity >= 0.5) and data collation yielding 1230 samples across 24 cancer types, plus per-cancer-type median normalization of mtDNA copy number to a median of one (repo: C7_Collate_mutation_data.ipynb, C8_normalize_MTCN_TotNumMut.R) — no software or version stated for this step

Functional association of the 49 nuclear mtDNA-copy-number regulator genes (from Gupta et al. 2023) using Gene Ontology cellular component, molecular function and biological process annotations, 'GO database (2024 version)' (repo: C6_functional_association/1_make_goterm_list.ipynb, 2_genelist_goterm_association.ipynb) — year-only database stamp, not an exact GO release

Spearman rank-correlation analysis of mtDNA copy number against total mutational load, nuclear SNVs, nuclear indels, mtDNA SNVs, mtDNA indels, specific nucleotide substitution types and APOBEC enrichment — pan-cancer on all 1230 samples and per cancer type restricted to types with >= 3 samples (21 types) (repo: C9_read_data_pancancer_corplot.R, C10_all_separate_Corr.R) — no R version, no package versions

Conversion of TNM staging to stages 1-4 per Rosen and Sapra (2023) and analysis of mtDNA copy number and mutational load variation across cancer stages (Fig. S30, S31) — no script identified in the repository listing for the TNM mapping, no version, no software named

Linear regression predicting mutational load from mtDNA copy number, fitted on an 80% training split and evaluated on the 20% test split by Spearman correlation of predicted vs actual (repo: C11_linreg_TotNumMut_mtDNA_CN.R, C12_LinearReg_model.R) — no RNG seed and no split procedure stated, no R version

Ridge regression of mtDNA copy number on 87 predictor features with the R package 'ridge' (Cule et al. 2022); parameters with p < 0.05 retained as key parameters and the final model refitted on key parameters only — no package version, no lambda selection procedure stated

Lasso regression of mtDNA copy number with the R package 'glmnet' (Friedman et al. 2010); non-zero-coefficient features retained, best lambda from a grid search with 10-fold cross-validation, final model refitted with key parameters and best lambda — no package version, no lambda grid range, no RNG seed for the CV folds

Random forest regression of mtDNA copy number with the R package 'randomForest' (Liaw and Wiener 2002) at 'default parameter values', feature ranking by importance, then 80/20 train/test prediction compared by Spearman correlation — 'default' is version-dependent and no package version or RNG seed is given

Download of PCAWG transcript-level expression data for 26 cancer types from the ICGC data portal and conversion to gene level by summing all expressed transcripts per gene, restricted to samples with tumor purity >= 0.5 (repo: C0_transcriptome_data_PCAWG_v2.pl) — controlled-access data, no release version or download date

Per-cancer-type split into low- and high-mtDNA samples at the cancer-type median mtDNA copy number, with exclusion of Breast-LobularCA, Cervix-AdenoCA and Eso-AdenoCA (fewer than three samples per class), leaving 23 cancer types (repo: C1_Separate_low_high_mtDNA_samples.ipynb, C2_transcript_Separate_low_high_mtDNA_samples.ipynb)

Differential expression between high- and low-mtDNA samples at gene and transcript level with the Bioconductor package DESeq2 (Love et al. 2014), significance at adjusted p < 0.1 (FDR < 10%, Benjamini-Hochberg) (repo: C3_Rcode_DiffExprAnalysis_automated.R, C4_Rcode_transcript_DiffExprAnalysis_automated.R) — no DESeq2 version, no Bioconductor release, no R version, no design formula or covariates stated in prose

Principal component analysis of the samples with the Bioconductor package 'PCAtools' (Blighe and Lun 2019) — no version, and no parameters at all (no transformation, no variance filtering, no component selection stated); no clearly corresponding script in the repository listing

Volcano plots generated with the R package 'EnhancedVolcano' (Blighe et al. 2018) — no version and no cutoffs, labelling rules or axis limits stated; no clearly corresponding script in the repository listing

Expression heatmaps generated with the R package 'pheatmap' (Kolde 2025) (repo heatmap scripts: C9_heatmap_msigdb_hallmarks.R, C10_heatmap_stats_pancancer.R, C12_heatmap_linreg_AllFeat_hallmark.R) — no version, and no scaling, clustering distance/linkage or gene-selection parameters stated in prose

Categorization of unique versus common differentially expressed genes by checking shared up-/down-regulation across two or more cancer types (repo: C5_gene_list_create.ipynb, C7_common_genes_cancer_types.ipynb) — no software or version stated

Inference of alternatively spliced genes: differentially expressed transcripts mapped to genes, and a gene called alternatively spliced when one or more transcripts are up-regulated and one or more down-regulated simultaneously (repo: C6_transcript_gene_mapping.ipynb, C8_alternative_splicing.ipynb) — criterion fully stated, but no transcript-to-gene annotation source or version given

Functional and pathway enrichment of alternatively spliced genes and of genes up-/down-regulated in two or more cancer types with g:Profiler version e113_eg59_p19_f6a03c19 (databases updated 2024) against GO Biological Process, KEGG and Reactome, filtering enriched classes at adjusted p < 0.1 (10% FDR) and computing fold enrichment — the only exact version string anywhere in the paper; no corresponding script in the repository listing

Per-cancer-type fold-change analysis of the 50 MSigDB hallmark gene sets (Liberzon et al. 2015) represented as heatmaps (repo: C9_heatmap_msigdb_hallmarks.R) — no MSigDB release version, no download date, no gene-set aggregation rule stated

EMT signature enrichment in low-mtDNA samples using the EMTome database (Vasaikar et al. 2021), restricted to the 10 pan-cancer signature gene sets, counting genes with adjusted p < 0.1 up in low- versus high-mtDNA samples and computing an enrichment score by the stated formula — no EMTome version or access date; no clearly corresponding script in the repository listing

Analysis of immune-response signature gene sets from the Reactome and BioCarta pathway maps in MSigDB — no version, no set list enumerated, no selection criterion stated; no clearly corresponding script in the repository listing

Per-gene linear regression predicting hallmark gene-set expression from MT-CO2 expression as an indicator of mitochondrial functional state: 80/20 train/test split per gene, prediction on the test set, Spearman correlation of predicted vs actual, reporting mean correlation and the number of genes with p < 0.05 (repo: C11_linreg_AllFeat_hallmark.R, C13_linreg_AllFeat_pred_hallmark.R) — no R version, no RNG seed, no normalization of expression stated

Chemotherapy-resistance likelihood score: patients with chemotherapy as first therapy and a known response, 'disease progression' classed resistant versus 'complete response'/'stable disease' classed responding, median normalization of mtDNA copy number across cancer types, binning into 10 equal-sized bins and computing the likelihood score per bin (no score for empty bins) (repo: 3_drug_response_resistance_risk.R) — no software or version stated

headline.static_readiness: 0/26 (0%) - stage1 ceiling only, no R-star (R-star needs stage-2 code verification)
headline.inference_inclusive_upper_bound: RI ceiling on only 2/26 computational steps: C4 (mutation mapping, which pins the GRCh37 assembly build and states the 1000 bp promoter window and the truncating/strong-effect/silent classification) and C21 (g:Profiler version e113_eg59_p19_f6a03c19 with the adjusted p < 0.1 cutoff). 21/26 steps cap at NI because no version is pinned for any locally run software: bedtools, R itself, DESeq2, ridge, glmnet, randomForest, PCAtools, EnhancedVolcano, pheatmap are all named without versions, and the PCAWG/ICGC, TCMA, GO, MSigDB and EMTome data resources carry no release version or download date. 3/26 steps are blocked (X) because the params axis is 0 as well as the version axis: PCA (PCAtools), volcano plots (EnhancedVolcano) and heatmaps (pheatmap) are named with no parameters whatsoever. A public analysis-code repository exists (github.com/riddhimandhar/Cancer_mtDNAcn, GPL-3.0, README maps three folders plus one top-level script onto the Methods subsections), so most steps have a code artifact, but the repository has no releases, no tags, and no environment, lockfile, container, conda spec, renv, or sessionInfo artifact of any kind. Capture claim is therefore floating, not exact_pins_partial.
headline.coverage: 26 computational steps assessed from the bioRxiv v1 JATS Methods (all eight Methods subsections) plus the repository README prose. W = 0: the paper reports no wet-lab work, all data are secondary consortium data (PCAWG/ICGC, TCMA). No step is out of scope.

gaps.where: Steps C1-C3, C5-C20, C22-C26 (every step except C4 and C21)
gaps.missing: No software version is pinned anywhere for locally run tools. bedtools, R, DESeq2, PCAtools, EnhancedVolcano, pheatmap, ridge, glmnet and randomForest are cited by reference only. The single exact version string in the whole paper is the g:Profiler service version e113_eg59_p19_f6a03c19 (step C21). 'GO database (2024 version)' and 'databases updated 2024' are year-only stamps, not exact releases.
gaps.how_to_close: State the exact version of R and of every package and command-line tool in Methods, and record sessionInfo() output alongside the scripts in the repository.

gaps.missing: No environment capture of any kind is claimed or present: the repository file listing contains only .R, .pl and .ipynb files plus LICENSE and README.md, with no renv.lock, DESCRIPTION, environment.yml, conda-lock, requirements.txt, Dockerfile, Singularity definition, or container digest. There is also no release and no tag, so the code state corresponding to the manuscript cannot be identified by any citable pointer.
gaps.how_to_close: Ship an renv.lock (or conda/pixi lockfile, or a container image with digest) covering the R/Bioconductor stack, Perl, and Jupyter/Python; tag a release matching the manuscript and archive it to Zenodo for a citable DOI.

gaps.where: Data availability statement; steps C1, C3, C13
gaps.missing: The PCAWG/ICGC genomic and transcriptomic data are stated to be 'available at the ICGC data portal post data access authorization' - controlled access, with no accession, no project identifier, no data release version, and no download date. The aligned normal-sample WGS/WXS read data used for the normal mtDNA copy-number calculation (C3) are likewise unspecified beyond 'as available for each cancer type'. TCMA is public but is given only as a landing-page URL with no release version. The collated intermediate dataset (1230 samples x 87 features, Table S2) is not deposited in a machine-readable form outside the supplementary tables.
gaps.how_to_close: State the ICGC/PCAWG data release version, the exact object/file list or manifest, and the download date; state the TCMA release; deposit the derived collated feature matrix and the per-cancer-type differential-expression result tables in a public archive (Zenodo/figshare) so the analysis has a citable, unrestricted entry point downstream of the controlled-access raw data.

gaps.missing: Parameter under-specification. No RNG seed or split procedure is given for any of the four 80/20 train/test splits (C9, C12, C25) or for the 10-fold cross-validation in Lasso (C11); the Lasso lambda grid range is not given; the Ridge lambda selection procedure is not described; randomForest is run at 'default parameter values' without a package version, so the defaults are not determinate; the DESeq2 design formula, covariates and filtering are not stated (C15); PCA, volcano and heatmap steps state no parameters at all (C16, C17, C18); the bedtools command line and coverage/mappability thresholds are absent (C3); the transcript-to-gene annotation source used for splicing inference is not named (C20); MSigDB/Reactome/BioCarta gene-set selection rules are not enumerated (C22, C24).
gaps.how_to_close: State every non-default parameter, threshold, RNG seed and annotation source in Methods, and set seeds explicitly in the published scripts.

gaps.where: Repository github.com/riddhimandhar/Cancer_mtDNAcn - coverage gaps and traceability
gaps.missing: The repository is public and its README maps folders onto Methods subsections, but there is no run order, no driver script, no input-path documentation, no expected-output description, and no figure-to-script mapping. Several Methods steps have no visibly corresponding script in the file listing: the TNM-to-stage conversion (C8), the g:Profiler enrichment runs (C21), the EMTome enrichment score (C23), the immune-signature analysis (C24), and the PCA/volcano plotting (C16, C17). Conversely, the repository contains ploidy-correction scripts (C13_Ploidy_corrections_data.R, C14_LinearReg_model_PloidyAdj_mtCN.R) that are not described in the Methods prose, so code and prose are not in one-to-one correspondence.
gaps.how_to_close: Add a run-order/driver script or workflow definition, document expected inputs and outputs per script, map each figure and table to the script that produces it, and either describe the ploidy-correction analysis in Methods or mark those scripts as exploratory.

gaps.where: Steps C16, C17, C18 - PCA, volcano plots, heatmaps
gaps.missing: These three steps name a package and nothing else. With neither a version nor any parameter, the visual outputs cannot be regenerated deterministically even given the input matrices, which is why they score params = 0 and are recorded as blocked rather than merely inference-requiring.
gaps.how_to_close: Publish the plotting scripts with explicit transformation, scaling, clustering distance/linkage, cutoff and labelling arguments, pinned to package versions.
